problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{2{x}^{2}+x-1}{3x+2}.$
worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2{x}^{2}+x-1}{3x+2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2{x}^{2}}{x}+\frac{x}{x}-\frac{1}{x})}{(\frac{3x}{x}+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(2x+1-\frac{1}{x})}{(3+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(2x+1-0)}{(3+0)} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(2x+1) \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
